claims.statement: Facebook Messenger inbound signatures are verified via X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC-SHA256 against the raw request body (re-serializing JSON breaks the signature), accepting both sha256=<hex> and bare hex forms; hmac.compare_digest makes the comparison constant-time, and a missing app secret returns SignatureVerification(verified=False, reason="app_secret_not_configured") rather than raising.

FacebookMessengerNormalizer converts one webhook POST's entry[]/messaging[] items into (inbound_messages, ignored_reason_counts): only candidate-initiated message.text becomes a ChannelInboundMessage; echoes, postbacks, quick replies without plain text, attachments, stickers, and reactions are ignored and surfaced via safe ignored-reason counts (no PII).

MESSENGER_STANDARD_WINDOW = timedelta(hours=24) is a code constant; evaluate_send_eligibility returns allowed=False with reason no_inbound_window (person never wrote) or window_expired (24h elapsed), and allowed=True with safe window_remaining_seconds for telemetry; V1 deliberately uses no relaxed policies.

OAuth requires pages_show_list, pages_manage_metadata, pages_messaging, public_profile (advanced access for go-live); the encrypted Page-selection flow is keyed by a server-generated state token and a flow id stored in FacebookOAuthStateStore / FacebookOAuthFlowStore; only FacebookPageSummary (id, name, tasks) crosses the boundary back to the admin UI — access tokens never do.

Per-Page tokens are persisted as facebook_page_token:<page_id> rows in integration_settings encrypted with AAD = page_id, resolved per turn via IntegrationSettingsService; the value is never serialized into API responses, logs, or queue payloads.

The shared ingress / graph / dispatch services never import facebook_messenger.py, facebook_oauth.py, or facebook_account.py — they resolve via the ChannelAccountResolver port; FacebookAccountResolver.active_facebook_page() is enforced single-active both in code and at the DB level by the partial unique index uq_channel_accounts_one_active_facebook_messenger from Alembic 0047.
